summary: Pass-through POP that does nothing, passes its input unchanged, and does not consume CPU or GPU memory. Use it as a named, stable POP reference endpoint while building or refactoring POP chains.

key_params.name: bypass
key_params.note: Bypass flag; bypassed operators output their first input unchanged.

common_gotchas: A Null POP itself does not consume CPU or GPU memory and passes unchanged data through, so performance issues usually belong upstream or downstream.
POP attributes that are not changed can remain references to the POP where they were last created or modified; check the middle-click popup info for the (r) marker.
Give the endpoint a meaningful Null POP name before referencing it downstream, so new POPs can be inserted upstream without reconnecting consumers.
Bypass is the only documented Null-page parameter; do not model generic cook or display controls as Null POP parameters.
